description:
Today the embargo for Nvidia's new RTX 2080 SUPER has lifted, and we're looking at the Founders Edition as well as MSI's Gaming X Trio custom card. Built on the same TU104 GPU as the original RTX 2080, this time with 128 more CUDA cores and faster memory, is the 2080 SUPER any good?

Read the full Founders Edition review here: http://bit.ly/32Iqg7E

Read the full MSI Gaming X Trio review here: http://bit.ly/32KmpHg

Check out KITGURU MERCH over here: https://teespring.com/en-GB/stores/kitguru-merch-store.

Be sure to support us on PATREON https://www.patreon.com/kitgurutech and read our MANTRA on HONEST REVIEWS Here: http://bit.ly/2BopnF9

comments.text: @Fiklm my 2080 memory hits 16. Im striking distance on overall performance of the 2080S. I also have the msi gaming x trio though, and its a beast. Frankly id settle for a bios that allowed more power limit than the 109 we get out of the box. I think i could match the super with my 2080 with higher tdp.as it sits its got access to 375w given the connectors and the pcie slot. But it only ever pulls 280-285w max.
comments.author: @BenFilley

comments.text: @Fiklm again though I'm just mostly interested in unlocked cores over the memory bump. Yeah that would be nice for the ones that were capable, but the cores are what im looking at. Whether the original 2080 die is limited through the bios, or if its at the silicon level. Its safe to say that if its the exact same silicon as the die name suggests, that the bios should open things up. At that point you can downlock the memory to 14 if you need to for stability, while still opening more cores.  You can also assume the reason they would have some locked away on the original 2080 would have been as simple as the process not having as high a yield in the working core sections across entire batches of chips, so they locked away some via bios and unlocked them later when the process had matured enough to get the yields of higher cores that they wanted. Which is where the super cards come in. Matured process, higher yields. You can assume many would not be up to the task though, I get that. Which is why we need a higher tdp bios for almost all 2080 cards.
